WR is breaking back toward the QB on a short comeback, but CB is already in front (3-4 yd lead along y) and moving much faster (6.6 vs 2.6). Separation 2.7 yd is not reliable for a clean throw making the catch with a bullet to settle point. The cushion is shrinking on a ball to the break point, so no safe window now; watch for a moment when WR plants and creates space as the CB commits to the under/over move.
t=2.0 Lock heading on break after the call and settle to catch; prepare for ball arrival.
WR upfield stem; maintain shadow, small x-tilt to track, no real cut yet. Keep cushion and ready for a potential real cut.

CB is closing upfield while WR is breaking back toward the QB; the CB's speed (6.6 yd/s) plus direction is driving separation to increase or stay far too small for a 1.8+ gap to develop before ball arrival. No clean window before t+0.3–2.5s; throw would likely be undercut or intercepted. Hold for a later window if cushion changes.

Ball is in air on the committed break path. Maintain heading to preserve throw target. Accelerate to close distance and reach landing zone in time while CB remains behind or off to the side. Facing toward expected catch direction helps alignment for the catch.
Real cut held by WR at 1.8s, switch to chase: mirror WR heading (225°) and close on intercept; ball not yet released.

WR open window (0.0-0.4s) cannot be satisfied with any arc release now, as all arcs meet the WR at +1.0s or more. Holding allows more time to time the throw so the ball arrives after a deeper separation and within the arc that safely clears the CB.
QB threw to 225° path. Maintain heading to catch, accelerate to close any remaining gap and reach landing zone as ball arrives.
Real WR cut detected; switch to normal and mirror WR heading to close the angle.
No arc arrives within the 0.0-0.6s window from now. All arcs meet at (13.8,60.0) with arrival times +1.0s to +1.9s. Hold to let WR settle into position and reassess after a shorter window or cushion.
QB threw to your heading; keep path to catch the ball. Use full acceleration to maintain separation as CB recovers. Do not alter heading until the ball arrives.
WR real cut established; flip to match and close on their heading. We are already aligned at 225°, maintain pursuit with full speed.

No arc arrives within the 0.0-0.6s window from now. All arcs would arrive after 1.0s+ (bullet 1.0s, drive 1.3s, touch 1.6s, loft 1.9s). Since the WR is open now but the throw would reach him after he may have moved or the CB could recover, we should hold and re-evaluate in the next moment to see if the window shifts or if the CB cushion collapses, allowing a refined throw. If later a window opens with a feasible arrival, we would select the flattest arc that lands within that window (prefer bullet), with target_coord near (13.4,59.6) and target_z around 1.5 (adjusted toward 2.5-3.0 only if the CB is unable to reach).

The route completed its break; separation is established. Do not change heading. Accelerate to reach the catch point while facing the anticipated ball landing zone at ~225°. This keeps you aligned with the throw and maximizes catch probability as CB recovers.
Real cut committed to 225°, continue mirroring on hip; maintain cushion and wait for WR to break, no extra corrections

WR is behind the CB by 4.2 yd and both are moving 225deg toward the QB. WR speed 6.1 vs CB 4.7 gives a closing rate of 1.4 yd/s. Time to close 4.2 yd separation ≈ 3.0 s, which is beyond the 2.6 s sack clock. A deep window cannot open before the CB would still be ahead or in cushion; a deep ball would require WR to pull even with/past the CB (≈3.0 s) and then to beat the cushion, which is not feasible within this clock. Therefore, no throwing window now; hold.

Ball is in flight toward our current heading. With separation established and QB throwing to landing zone, maintain heading 225° and face toward the ball, accelerate to reach catch window within 0.3-0.5s while tracking landing spot.
WR made a real cut; switch to normal mode and mirror their heading (225°) to close with full burst availability

WR open window 0.0-0.4s from now is not matched by any arc arrival (all arcs would arrive at +1.0s to +1.9s). CB is closing; delay and reassess after path progression or adjust timing to hit the earlier window.

WR behind CB but faster; both moving toward QB on 225deg. Separation is already 4.4 yd but the CB has the high ground and cushion is shrinking as they converge. With a 0.3-2.5s throw window required for a 1.8+ separation, projection shows the gap will likely shrink or stay around current level rather than widen. No clean window to deep-ball past the CB; hold to see if separation improves after the break as WR plants.
